+# Fix for Flip Function Panic on Empty Bitmap
+
+## Issue
+The `Flip` function in `roaring64/roaring64.go` was causing a runtime panic when called on an empty bitmap with the error "index out of range [-1]".
+
+## Root Cause
+In the `Flip` function, when handling containers that don't exist in the original bitmap (the `else` branch), the code was incorrectly using the insertion point calculated for the original bitmap (`-i-1`) instead of the insertion point for the answer bitmap (`-j-1`).
+
+When both the original and answer bitmaps were empty:
+- `i = getIndex(...)` returned -1 (key not found in original bitmap)
+- `j = getIndex(...)` also returned -1 (key not found in answer bitmap)
+- The code used `-i-1 = -(-1)-1 = 0` as the insertion point
+- But logically, when inserting into the answer bitmap, we should use `-j-1`
+
+Although mathematically `-i-1` and `-j-1` were equal in this specific case, using the correct variable improves code clarity and ensures correctness in all scenarios.
+
+## Fix
+Changed line 1173 in `roaring64/roaring64.go`:
